title: Rate Limiter
statement:
An API gateway allows each client at most `limit` requests in any window of
`window` milliseconds. Requests arrive in time order as millisecond timestamps.
A request at time `t` is accepted when fewer than `limit` requests have been
**accepted** in the half-open interval `(t - window, t]`; otherwise it is
dropped. Dropped requests do not count toward the window.

Return how many requests are dropped.

**Example 1**

`dropped_requests([0, 10, 20, 30], 2, 25)` returns `1`: the third request finds
two accepted ones within the last 25ms and is dropped; by 30ms the first has
aged out, so the fourth is accepted.

**Example 2**

`dropped_requests([5, 5, 5], 1, 1)` returns `2`.

**Constraints**

- `0 <= timestamps.length <= 100000`, non-decreasing
- `1 <= limit <= 100000`
- `1 <= window <= 10^12`
- `0 <= timestamps[i] <= 10^15`, so they need a 64-bit integer
guidelines: A queue of accepted timestamps, evicting from the front. The subtleties are the half-open window (a request exactly one window later is allowed in), and that dropped requests must not be enqueued, which the third sample-style case checks. Ask how they would make this work across several gateway instances.

test_cases.name: one short of a window apart
